question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme in Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing the salaries of hospital pharmacy staff
options.B: Eliminating the need for private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Importing expensive foreign drugs for specialized care
options.D: Ensuring safe and affordable medicines are always available

explanation: The primary objective is to make safe, effective, and affordable medications accessible to the general public within the health system. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why does the healthcare system focus on a specific list of essential medicines?

options.A: To make drug manufacturing easier for local herbalists
options.B: To restrict patients from using modern medical treatments
options.C: To maximize scarce financial resources for priority health needs
options.D: To completely stop the importation of foreign medical goods

explanation: Using a focused list ensures limited budgets target the most critical health conditions affecting the population. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h1)

question: What data helps nurses and pharmacists calculate accurate drug quantification needs?

options.A: The market value of shares in private drug companies
options.B: Consumption rates and local disease morbidity data
options.C: International travel trends of pharmaceutical executives
options.D: The personal preference of the hospital medical director

explanation: Accurate quantification relies heavily on tracking past consumption patterns and the actual disease burden in the community. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h2)

question: A ward nurse notices a sudden spike in malaria cases during the rainy season. What action supports proper quantification?

options.A: Reporting the increased consumption to help adjust future drug orders
options.B: Telling patients to buy unverified herbal remedies from the market
options.C: Stopping the administration of anti-malarial drugs entirely
options.D: Hiding the remaining stock of antimalarials in a personal locker

explanation: Ward nurses observe real-time disease trends and consumption spikes, which inform accurate future quantification and prevent shortages. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h2)

question: What does the FEFO inventory principle stand for in pharmacy supply management?
explanation: FEFO ensures that medications closest to their expiration date are used first to minimize financial loss and patient risk. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why must ward nurses regularly check and record storage temperatures for vaccines and insulins?

options.A: To ensure the electricity bill is paid on time by the hospital
options.B: To prevent heat exposure from degrading the active ingredients
options.C: To make the pharmacy store room look neat and organized
options.D: To comply with international fashion and design standards

explanation: Temperature excursions can destroy the potency of cold-chain items like vaccines and insulin, making them ineffective. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is a major consequence of the irrational use and overprescription of antibiotics?

options.A: Lower financial costs for the patient family
options.C: Faster healing times for viral infections
options.D: Immediate reduction in hospital admission rates

explanation: Overusing or misusing antibiotics allows microbes to adapt and develop resistance, rendering standard treatments ineffective. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h4)

question: A nurse is about to give a medication prescribed by the doctor. Which check is essential to promote rational and safe drug use?

options.A: Checking which drug brand has the most colorful packaging
options.B: Asking the patient for a cash tip before administration
options.C: Ignoring hospital treatment guidelines to save time
options.D: Verifying the right patient, dose, route, and time

explanation: Standard rights of medication administration protect patients from dosing errors and ensure safe, targeted therapy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do patients frequently stop taking their prescribed medications prematurely?

options.A: They prefer to take bitter traditional herbs instead
options.B: They feel better and assume the illness is completely cured
options.C: They receive daily phone calls from the hospital pharmacist
options.D: They have unlimited financial resources to buy more drugs

explanation: Symptom resolution often tricks patients into believing the treatment course is finished, leading to non-adherence especially with antibiotics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h5)

question: How can a nurse best support a patient who is confused about taking multiple daily medications?

options.A: Hiding the pill bottles to reduce the patient anxiety
options.B: Yelling at the patient for failing to read the medical textbook
options.C: Telling the patient to stop all drugs until next month
options.D: Providing clear, simple instructions and practical reminders

explanation: Clear guidance and practical adherence aids help patients manage complex drug regimens safely at home. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: Detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse drug reactions
options.B: Selling expired drugs to local patent medicine vendors
options.C: Designing colorful packaging for new pharmaceutical products
options.D: Increasing the market price of imported medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance monitors drug safety post-market to catch and manage harmful or unexpected side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h6)

question: A patient develops a severe skin rash shortly after receiving a newly introduced antibiotic. What is the immediate nursing duty?

options.A: Stop the drug, provide supportive care, and report the reaction
options.B: Ignore the rash because it will disappear without treatment
options.C: Double the dose of the antibiotic to test if the rash worsens
options.D: Blame the patient for having sensitive skin and walk away

explanation: Suspected adverse reactions require immediate cessation of the offending agent, patient stabilization, and official reporting to authorities like NAFDAC. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h6)
